records.question: How did the average rate of land subsidence on Tutuila change after the 2009 Samoa-Tonga earthquake doublet according to the section?
records.ground_truth_answer: It increased from an average rate of 1–2 mm/year prior to 2009 to an average rate of 16 mm/year during the period after the earthquakes (2009–201[76](#page-10-5)).
ground_truth_chunks: Based on NOAA's Pago Pago tide gauge, satellite altimetry, and Global Navigation Satellite System land motion data, it was found that prior to the 2009 Samoa-Tonga earthquake doublet, land subsidence of Tutuila was occurring at an average rate of 1–2 mm/year.
Afer the earthquakes, average rates of land subsidence increased to 16 mm/year during the period of 2009–201[76](#page-10-5) .

records.question: What cross-shore grid spacing, cross-shore extent, and alongshore sampling were used for the numerical model's bathymetry transect?
records.ground_truth_answer: A 500-m long, 1-dimensional grid from 32-m water depth to 10 m above MSL was used, with cross-shore grid spacing varying from 2 m at the seaward boundary to 0.04 m at the shoreward boundary (linear interpolation). The input bathymetry had 3 grid points in the alongshore direction with 1-m spacing and each cross-shore transect was identical; the single transect was derived from an average of parallel cross-shore transects spanning 100 m in the alongshore, spaced every 2 m.
ground_truth_chunks: For the numerical modeling described in subsequent sections, we use a 500-m long, 1-dimensional grid from 32-m water depth to 10 m above MSL.
We vary the cross-shore grid spacing from 2 m at the seaward boundary to 0.04 m at the shoreward boundary using linear interpolation.

The input bathymetry has 3 grid points in the alongshore direction with 1-m spacing, and each cross-shore transect is identical. This single transect is derived from an average of parallel cross-shore transects spanning 100 m in the alongshore, spaced every 2 m (Fig. 1c).

records.question: According to the SWASH modeling in this Discussion section, how does the maximum nearshore sea-swell (SS) significant wave height vary with water depth at the reef crest?
records.ground_truth_answer: The model predicts the maximum nearshore SS significant wave height increases quadratically with water depth; additionally, once water levels exceed about 1.2 m mean water depth, dependence on offshore wave height increases because smaller waves can propagate across the reef without breaking.
ground_truth_chunks: We find that the model predicts that the maximum nearshore SS significant wave height for a given water depth increases quadratically with water depth.
As water levels exceed ~1.2 m mean water depth, the dependence on offshore wave height increases as smaller waves are able to propagate across the reef without breaking.
